newsitem.title: GERMANY: German opposition postpones visit to Iran.
newsitem.headline: German opposition postpones visit to Iran.

text.p: Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD) said on Tuesday they had postponed a visit of parliamentary deputies to Iran scheduled for the end of the week, but gave no reasons for the decision.
The SPD said it had made the decision in "mutual agreement" with the Iranian ambassador in Bonn, Hossein Mousavian.

It said in a statement Mousavian met the SPD deputy leader in parliament, Guenter Verheugen, on Monday to discuss relations between the two countries, but gave no further details of what they talked about.

Iran's relationship with Germany -- Tehran's main European trading partner -- have become strained in recent months by a pending German court decision on the 1992 killings of three Kurdish dissidents and their translator in a Berlin restaurant.
Prosecutors have accused Iran of ordering the killings, but Iran denies any involvement.
Ties are also under pressure over the case of an Iranian journalist Faraj Sarkuhi arrested by Iranian authorities for allegedly trying to leave the country illegally.
Bonn has asked Tehran to explain reports that Sarkuhi was detained and tortured for 47 days last year when he was supposed to be in Germany.
Tehran has accused Germany of what it calls interference in the case which it said is an internal affair.
